Having been a juror, I'll shed some light on the situation for those who's only experience of court is a TV drama. No, it's nothing like what you see on TV.

The opening statement basically goes something like this. The Judge starts by explaining to the Jury that the lawyers will now paint a picture of their personal opinion of the case, give a basic road map of where they expect to take the case, and that nothing they say is actual evidence.

Then the lawyers will get up and give some passioned speech while an assistant stares at you. Really really stares at you hard to see what emotions you react to. The assistant will note down even the slightest twitch so the lawyer knows what buttons to push later in the trial, for the sake of manipulation, when the evidence is finally presented in it's proper place.

Anyway, the speech will be just a few minutes and go something like this... "I believe the defendant is guilty. During this trial I will present evidence of his guilt. We have such and such video evidence and such and such witnesses and you will see the evidence and witnesses later." That's basically what an opening statement is supposed to be.

So, actually presenting evidence during an opening statement will completely throw off the defense in such a way that it would be unfair. Why? Because now the defense has to switch from an opening statement to refuting the prosecution, which was never the point of an opening statement in the first place. An opening statement isn't a debate. It's just a roadmap the two sides want to travel during the proceedings of the trial.
